# Figure workbench audit acceptance

## D0 fixture and provenance

The workbench implementation uses Citrus renderer IDs, the verified artifact digest, the existing account-scoped revision and override pipeline, and Chromium's SVG geometry. Tavotto commit `595e5182b8579adc4bfece2b72ca0adee0a427fb` (AGPL-3.0-only) supplied the published behaviors and acceptance criteria. No Tavotto source or dependency was used. [Behavior reference](https://github.com/Tavotto/Tavotto/blob/595e5182b8579adc4bfece2b72ca0adee0a427fb/docs/adr/0086-precise-hit-geometry-for-series-shapes-and-annotations.md)

D acceptance uses a synthetic TSS reconstruction with three exactly overlapping line, marker and errorbar series. Its repeated input gives each group the same nonzero sample standard deviation. It uses sample data generated by the fixture. The production TSS source and account projects were not used. The test also renders a Matplotlib two-panel frozen script, writes a separate PNG fixture and builds a static SVG through the ordinary safe parser. `workbench-d-ggplot.R` runs actual pinned R 4.4.3, ggplot2 4.0.4 and svglite 2.2.2. The fixture-generated R SVG SHA-256 is `5067fe077d2ca7149af51881b664b8569b6781edd488a5e4a685e391526c76f1` in the recorded environment.

Run `workbench-d-ggplot.R` with `/opt/citrus-r/bin/Rscript --vanilla` inside the pinned R sandbox. Make a temporary, private fixture data directory and two named pipes. Run `python -m src.figures.workbench.d_audit_fixture <data directory> <R SVG> <requests FIFO> <responses FIFO>` from the application SIF with `01_src`, `packages` and the pinned pytest dependencies on `PYTHONPATH`. Run `workbench-d-audit-chromium.py <requests FIFO> <responses FIFO> <output directory> --chromium <pinned executable>` from the sealed Playwright environment with Playwright and PIL on `PYTHONPATH`. Bind the repository's web tree read-only and mount the temporary data separately. The browser intercepts the synthetic HTTP origin and gets application route responses over the pipes. The fixture starts no HTTP listener, uses a test-only account/registry and writes captures and timing data under the supplied output directory.

## D1, D2 and D3 coverage

- D1 binds the workbench's canonical group identity to validated SVG addresses, clip references, paint order, capability and read-only information, render revision and exact render digest. Selection and highlight use the painted object. Real Chromium covers overlaid errors and markers, Alt cycling, blank areas, even-odd fill, dashed stroke, clipping, transparent paint, canvas zoom 125/150/190%, scrolling, and a 390px viewport. At 390px, separate real mouse and touch contexts click actual R ink after scrolling at 190% canvas zoom and focus the properties drawer without overflowing the viewport. Duplicate SVG IDs and object-contract entries with the wrong identity, revision or digest disable picking while preserving the exact preview and the tree. An asset digest mismatch discards the SVG and can show the separately verified PNG. A separate Matplotlib fixture selects one annotation arrow, one standalone arrow and one standalone patch from their renderer-emitted SVG paths. These are inspection-only, do not change the v1 replay target list and are not inferred for older SVGs.
- D2 verifies a changed screenshot and actual title-node transform before pointer release. No draft request occurs during the gesture. One request follows release, one undo restores the saved offset, and Escape resets a subsequent in-flight gesture. The color dialog provides an HSV surface and keyboard sliders, hexadecimal and RGB inputs, original and current colors, cancel, and recent colors. Radio grids represent line and marker shapes. Marker fill mode is independent from color and opacity. Color and marker control changes submit only when applied.
- D3 verifies source hash rejection, concurrent revision rejection and explicit rebase only when the source digest and exact group IDs still match. Reopen, saved version export, frozen Matplotlib source, and isolation between subplots are checked. R saves replay against the authorized original svglite bytes and registered paint overrides. Native R shapes support paint and line width where present. Text permits its existing fill color through the tree. Glyph paths and font metrics carry no font-editing capability. Registered ordinary SVG uses the existing independent editor after the safe parser succeeds. Registered PNG only advertises viewing and export. Raster layout/crop/annotations, JPEG project import, multi-panel composition tools, physical page templates, and TIFF have no D-series acceptance here. Legacy errorbar groups without emitted member metadata use their existing tree capability until a verified redraw supplies member addresses. Objects with unsupported or ambiguous browser geometry remain tree-only. A preview-worker change was not needed for the local gesture.

## Measurements

The final recorded focused run on the fixed desktop Chromium fixture logged `/home/WZQ/citrusscholar/preflight/audit-d-chromium.9EPHiKyB/output/metrics.json`. The measurements are fixture observations, with small sample counts and no running-service latency. The pointer timing is from the browser pointer handler to a callback after the local update in the same animation frame. It measures neither display presentation nor total raster/compositor cost.

| Measurement | Synthetic TSS p50 / p95 (ms) | R ggplot2 p50 / p95 (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Open to visible asset, 5 per fixture | 271.55 / 603.43 | 264.62 / 322.82 |
| Click to highlight DOM, 12 TSS; Playwright click to selected, 5 R | 1.90 / 10.52 | 7.78 / 9.63 |
| Pointer event to post-update rAF callback, 18 | 0.20 / 0.83 | No editable R drag |
| Authoritative draft through ASGI pipe, 6 per fixture | 917.00 / 935.01 | 24.18 / 37.65 |
| Saved receipt through ASGI pipe, 6 per fixture | 1075.31 / 1280.30 | 101.61 / 107.70 |

The real main browser run additionally exercised color and saved exports through the UI. The separate mixed experience suite passed 59 checks with zero console errors, including exact saved SVG download bytes. In the pinned application SIF the workbench Python tests passed 35 with seven skips for optional external evidence. Node checked all workbench modules and ran both browser SHA-256 paths against the independent OpenSSL-backed output on 11 inputs each.
